THE HERODS
Which Herod this is
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea "in the days of Herod the king", when wise men came from the east to Jerusalem asking, "Where is he that is born King of the Jews?" Matthew 2:1–2

"When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him." He asked the chief priests and scribes where Christ should be born, and they answered, "In Bethlehem of Judaea." Matthew 2:3–6
He called the wise men privately, "enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared", and sent them to Bethlehem: "bring me word again, that I may come and worship him also." Matthew 2:7–8

Warned of God in a dream, the wise men did not return to Herod. An angel told Joseph, "Herod will seek the young child to destroy him", and the family fled into Egypt "until the death of Herod". Matthew 2:12–15

When he saw that he was mocked, he "was exceeding wroth" and "slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under", reckoning by the time the wise men had given him. Matthew 2:16
"But when Herod was dead", Matthew says, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt: "they are dead which sought the young child's life." Matthew 2:19–20
Luke dates the angel's announcement to Zacharias "in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea". Luke 1:5

From the textScripture gives Herod no regnal record: no length of reign, no verdict formula, no burial. Everything it says of him belongs to the accounts of the births of John the Baptist and Jesus. Matthew 2:1–22 Luke 1:5

THE NATION
What the nation did
Herod gathered "all the chief priests and scribes of the people" to ask where Christ should be born. Matthew 2:4
The temple of Jesus' day had been "Forty and six years" in building, the Jews said to Jesus at Jerusalem. John does not name the builder. John 2:20

Scholars' viewSchürer (1890) dates the start of Herod's rebuilding to the end of 20 or the beginning of 19 BC; counting the forty-six years from then, he places that Passover of John 2 in AD 27 or, "more probably", AD 28. John 2:20 [7]

Prophets of the reign

Je Jeremiah “In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.”

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
None. Matthew and Luke date events by his reign (Matthew 2:1; Luke 1:5) but give no years.
SCHÜRER (1890)
Made king by the Roman Senate late in 40 BC; took Jerusalem in 37 BC; died at Jericho shortly before the Passover of 4 BC.
A LATER DEATH: 3 BC OR 1 BC (MINORITY, AS LISTED BY SCHÜRER)
No years given[8]
Quandt and Kellner put his death in 3 BC; Caspari and Riess in 1 BC (Schürer, 1890, p. 466, lists them without their reasons).
3 BC
Quandt and Kellner, as listed by Schürer (1890)
Schürer names them as placing the death a year later; he does not set out their reasons.[8]
1 BC
Caspari and Riess (1880), as listed by Schürer (1890)
Schürer names them as diverging further, to 1 BC (and Seyffarth further still, to AD 1); he does not set out their reasons.[8]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
Matthew 2 Luke 1 John 2 Acts 23
PASSAGES · 4
Matthew 2:1–23 Luke 1:5 John 2:20 Acts 23:35
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never calls him "the Great".
Scripture gives no length of reign, no verdict formula and no burial for Herod.
Matthew does not say how many children died at Bethlehem.
Scripture does not say how Herod died or where he was buried.
The Gospels do not say who rebuilt the temple of Jesus' day; John 2:20 gives only its forty-six years of building.
Matthew does not say how long after the birth the wise men came; Herod's "two years old and under" is reckoned from the time of the star.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textMatthew calls him only "Herod the king" and Luke "Herod, the king of Judaea". Matthew ties him to the rest of the family in one phrase: Archelaus reigned "in the room of his father Herod". Matthew 2:1 Luke 1:5 Matthew 2:22

Scholars' view"Herod's judgment hall" at Caesarea, where Paul was kept, is taken by commentators to be the palace Herod the Great had built there and the governors later used (Poole, 1683; Meyer, English translation 1877–1879; Vincent, 1887). Acts does not say which Herod built it. Acts 23:35 [32][21][30]
